property_summary: After calling `addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue` with an empty array, the reference sets `maxNodeDelegatorCount` via `updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount` and the new limit is reflected; the mutant ignores the assignment, so the old default `0` persists.

After initializing maxNodeDelegatorCount to 10, calling updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount(5) then addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with 6 new delegators: the reference reverts (exceeds limit 5) while the buggy version succeeds because maxNodeDelegatorCount stays 10.

After reducing maxNodeDelegatorCount from 10 to 2 via updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount(2), calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with 3 new delegators reverts in the reference (exceeds new limit) but succeeds in the buggy version (limit remains 10).

After initializing the contract, setting maxNodeDelegatorCount to 5 via updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount, then calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with 6 new addresses, the reference reverts (exceeds limit 5) while the mutant succeeds (limit stays 10).

After setting maxNodeDelegatorCount to 5 via updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with 6 new delegators reverts in the reference (exceeds limit 5) but succeeds in the buggy version (limit stays 10).
After initializing and calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with empty array, the reference contract leaves maxNodeDelegatorCount=10, while the buggy one sets it to 0.

After initializing and adding one node delegator contract (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10, queue length 1), calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an array of length 10 reverts on the reference because it exceeds maxNodeDelegatorCount (10 + 1 > 10), but succeeds on the bug where maxNodeDelegatorCount was set to 0 by updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount (1 + 10 > 0 is true, so it doesn't revert).

After initializing and adding one node delegator, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an array of length 10 reverts on the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10, total would be 11 > 10) but succeeds on the buggy version (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0, 11 > 0 is false, so it doesn't revert).

After initializing and adding one node delegator, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an array of length 9 reverts on reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10, 1+9>10) but succeeds on buggy version (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0, 1+9>0 is false).

After initializing and calling updateMaxNodeDelegatorCount with 0, the reference sets maxNodeDelegatorCount to 0 (as per parameter), but the bug sets it to 0 anyway; however the difference is that the bug always sets it to 0 regardless of the parameter. The test uses addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an empty array to trigger the divergence check.

After initialization, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with one address succeeds in the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10) but reverts in the bug (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0, since the line setting it to 10 was deleted).

After initialization with 0 ether, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with a non-zero address array of length 1 reverts in the bug (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0) but succeeds in the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10).

After initialization, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an array of 1 non-zero address fails in the buggy version (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0) but succeeds in the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10).

After initialization, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with an array of 1 non-zero address succeeds in the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10) but reverts in the bug (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0, since the line setting it to 10 was deleted).

After initialization, calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with one address succeeds in the reference (maxNodeDelegatorCount=10) but reverts in the bug (maxNodeDelegatorCount=0 because the line setting it to 10 was deleted).

After adding a node delegator via addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue, getTotalAssetDeposits(asset) returns a larger value (including node delegator balance) in the reference than in the buggy version (which returns only deposit pool balance), for a zero-balance delegator where only the deposit pool holds the asset.

After adding a node delegator via addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue and funding it with the asset, the reference getTotalAssetDeposits includes the delegator's balance while the buggy version only returns the deposit pool balance.

After adding a node delegator via addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue and funding both the deposit pool and the delegator with the same asset, the reference getTotalAssetDeposits includes the delegator's balance while the buggy version returns only the deposit pool balance, causing a divergence in the returned value.

After adding a node delegator via addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue and funding the delegator with an asset, getTotalAssetDeposits returns the sum of deposit pool and delegator balance in the reference but only the deposit pool balance in the buggy version.

After calling addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with a valid node delegator address and funding that delegator with 100 tokens, getTotalAssetDeposits returns (deposit pool balance + delegator balance) = 200 in the reference but only deposit pool balance = 100 in the buggy version.

After adding two node delegators and depositing 10 ETH into the deposit pool, getTotalAssetDeposits returns 30 (10 in pool + 10 in ndc1 + 10 in ndc2) in reference but only 20 in bug (ignores pool and staked amounts).

After adding a node delegator and depositing 10 ether into the deposit pool, getTotalAssetDeposits returns 10 (pool) + 0 (NDC balance) + 0 (staked) = 10 in reference but 0 in bug because bug ignores pool balance.

After adding two node delegators and depositing 20 ETH into the deposit pool, getTotalAssetDeposits returns 20 (pool) + 0 (NDC balances) + 0 (staked) = 20 in reference but 0 in bug because bug returns only assetLyingInNDCs which is 0.

After adding two node delegators and depositing 10 ETH into the deposit pool, getTotalAssetDeposits returns 30 (10 in pool + 10 in ndc1 + 10 in ndc2) in reference but only 20 in bug (ignores pool and staked amounts).

After adding a node delegator and depositing 10 WEI of an ERC20 token into the deposit pool, the reference's getTotalAssetDeposits returns 10 (pool only) while the bug returns 0 (ignores pool balance).

After adding a node delegator address to the queue, getTotalAssetDeposits returns the sum of assetLyingInDepositPool, assetLyingInNDCs, and assetStakedInEigenLayer in the reference, but only assetStakedInEigenLayer in the bug, causing a mismatch when the deposit pool has a positive balance of the asset.

After adding a node delegator contract to the queue, transferring an asset to it, then calling getTotalAssetDeposits on that asset, the reference returns the sum of deposit pool balance, node delegator balance, and staked amount, while the buggy version returns only the staked amount, causing a divergence when the deposit pool has a positive balance.

After adding a node delegator contract to the queue and transferring an ERC20 asset to it, getTotalAssetDeposits returns the sum of all three components (deposit pool balance, node delegator balance, staked amount) in the reference, but only the staked amount in the bug, causing a mismatch when both the deposit pool and node delegator hold a positive balance of the asset.

After adding a node delegator contract to the queue, the reference getTotalAssetDeposits returns the sum of deposit pool balance, node delegator balance, and staked amount, while the buggy version returns only the staked amount, causing a divergence when the deposit pool holds a positive balance of the asset.

After adding a node delegator contract to the queue and supplying the deposit pool with an ERC20 asset, getTotalAssetDeposits returns the sum of deposit pool balance, node delegator balance, and staked amount in the reference, but only the staked amount in the bug, causing a mismatch when the deposit pool has a positive balance and the node delegator balance is zero.
After adding a node delegator contract with some balance of an asset, getTotalAssetDeposits returns a different value because the bug subtracts the node delegator's balance instead of adding it.
After adding a node delegator contract that holds some tokens, getTotalAssetDeposits returns a different value because the bug subtracts node delegator balances instead of adding them.
After adding a node delegator with a non-zero token balance, getTotalAssetDeposits returns a smaller value in the buggy version because it subtracts assetLyingInNDCs instead of adding it.

After adding a node delegator contract with a positive balance of an asset, getTotalAssetDeposits returns a larger value in the reference than in the buggy version because the bug subtracts assetLyingInNDCs instead of adding it.

When a node delegator with a non-zero balance of an asset is added, getTotalAssetDeposits returns (deposit pool + node delegator + staked) in reference but (deposit pool - node delegator + staked) in the bug, causing a difference that is observable via a public getter.
